item.title: Could a hidden planet twice Earth's mass explain strange orbits beyond Neptune?
item.description: In the cold, dark Kuiper belt region beyond Neptune, some icy bodies travel on steeply tilted paths, while others stay far from the giant planets even at their closest approach to the sun. A simulation study suggests that a hidden planet about twice Earth's mass could help explain both populations of objects.
